meta_description: FilmDesk is an Android logbook for film photographers: rolls, film stock, cameras, labs and your scans in one place. No ads, no tracking, backup to your own Google Drive.
og_description: Rolls, film stock, gear, labs and your scans in one place. Coming soon to Google Play.
lead: FilmDesk keeps your rolls, the film in your fridge, your cameras and lenses, the labs you trust and your scans together in one place. Works offline. No sign-up, no ads.
hero_meta: Free to use · Pro is a one-time purchase · Android 8 and up · 7 languages
f1_p: Camera, lens, film, lab and dates for each roll, with your scans laid out as a film strip.
f1_l1: Pick a cover frame for each roll
f1_l2: Rescan at another lab and keep both versions
f1_l3: A frame counter on every roll, like 32/36 EXP
f2_p: Every roll you own, from unshot to scanned. The status moves on its own as you log and scan.
f2_l1: Expiry reminders so no roll goes to waste
f3_p: Cameras, lenses and accessories with a photo of each, the rolls you shot on them, and the labs you trust.
f3_l1: Lab phone number, map link and which rolls went where
f3_l2: Service log: CLAs, light seals, repairs
f4_t: Albums and your year in film
f4_p: Gather your best frames into albums with captions, and see your rolls, stocks and cameras year by year. Share it as an image.
v_p: FilmDesk has no server. Your logbook lives on your phone, and backup goes to a folder in your own Google Drive that you control.
p1_s: FilmDesk keeps a safe copy of each scan and never edits your original photos.
p2_s: Photos and your logbook go to a "FilmDesk" folder. Optional, Wi‑Fi only.
p3_s: The app only adds files. Removing a roll on your phone leaves Drive as it is.
p4_s: No account, no analytics, no developer server. This website has no tracking either.
pro_note: Rescans don't count toward the 7 rolls. Viewing, editing, backup and restore are always free, and nothing you made is ever locked away.
q1: Why does FilmDesk ask for photo access?
a1: To check whether the original of each scan is still on your phone, so the app can warn you before you lose it and pick the right file to back up.
q2: When do my photos go to Google Drive?
a2: When you're on Wi‑Fi and the battery isn't low. A small cloud mark on each photo shows whether it's uploaded or waiting.
q3: I got a new phone. How do I get my logbook back?
a3: Install FilmDesk, answer "Used FilmDesk before?" and restore from your Drive. Pro comes back with the same Google account.
a4: No. Pro is a single purchase. Even without Pro, everything you made stays viewable and editable.
f4_l1: Yearly stats and a share image, free
f4_l2: Home screen photo widget, like a polaroid
